newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JULY 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JULY 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou laid out the principles of the 1998 budget to Prime Minister Costas Simitis at their meeting on Tuesday. Incomes policy for the public sector will involve wage increases of no more than 4.0 percent, there will be a contained indexation of the tax scale as well as a reduction in the interest rates for bonds by up to 2.5 percent, given a corresponding fall in inflation.

--Greek commerce is proposing that the government legislate to allow the right for a full-time position to be turned into two or more part-time positions. The proposal was forwarded to the committee on social dialogue to make changes to the job market, which met on Tuesday.

--The Athens Chamber of Commerce has objected to the relxation of pecuniary measures for bad cheques. The amendment foresees changing prevailing provisions which impose a 2-5 year sentence and allows offenders to pay off the jail term at a rate of 400-1,000 drachmas per day.

--Simitis brought up issues concerning the state-run electricity supplier DEH and the placing of a contract for a new unit at Florina, in northern Greece, with Development Minister Vasso Papandreou at their meeting on Tuesday.

--The national economy ministry is stepping up procedures to transfer funds totalling some 500 billion drachmas in an effort to improve the absorption rates of Community Support Framework funds, according to reports.
--A foreign consortium will begin searching for oil in western Greece by September at the latest, following the signing on Tuesday of a total 37 million dollar contract with the Greek state.
--Credit expansion to the private sector is continuing at high rates, according to the Bank of Greece, while credit growth to the public sector is contained.

--The government's economic sights are set on an inflation rate of below 2.0 percent by end-1999, with inflation to reach 3.0 percent next year with public deficits as 3.0 percent of GDP in 1998, which would allow Greece to maintain its hopes for inclusion in economic and monetary union in 1999.

--The weight of the government's economic policy will fall on inflation next year, Papandoniou told reporters after his meeting with the prime minister on Tuesday. Papandoniou said he wanted to push inflation down to below 3.0 percent next year from the 5.2-5.3 percent it is expected to close at this year.

--The committee on private insurance discussed the withdrawal of operating licences for two insurance firms at its session on Tuesday as well as the issue of how to deal with over-estimations of damage by insurance firms.
--Some 750 applications totalling 15.5 billion drachmas were submitted in first-half 1997 for support for young business entrepreneurs and the creation of small and medium-size enterprises.

--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, is hoping to decide on contracts and the realisation of a Fast Truck investment programme worth 135 billion drachmas by the end of July. Decisions on new contracts for between 600,00-1,800,000 digital switches are scheduled for next week. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
